title.narrative: Building Skills for Human Capital Development in South Sudan

description.narrative: The Project's Development Objective is to increase skills development opportunities in teaching and digital agriculture and strengthen capacity for management of the education system.

The proposed Project would support South Sudan to establish the minimum skills base needed to enable the country to accelerate human capital formation. The Project proposes to do this by addressing skills constraints in key sectors that contribute to human capital—education and agriculture. In both these sectors, lack of critical skills is a binding constraint for improving sector performance and will need to be addressed to enable complementary investments to produce returns. The Project would tackle these constraints by (i) enhancing teachers skills to strengthen education delivery through in-service and pre-service professional development; (ii) fostering the development of digital skills in youth through the piloting of a blended education model for a digital agriculture program and providing internet connectivity to ten public universities/polytechnic institutes; and (iii) strengthening local capacity to manage the education system by providing technical assistance and capacity building support to the Ministry of General Education and Instruction and Ministry of Higher Education, Science and Technology, strengthening information management systems, and establishing Project Implementation Units to manage Project activities. The Project will also finance activities to increase schooling opportunities in refugee hosting areas of South Sudan and promote inclusion of refugee children in these schools.

condition.narrative: Schedule 2 Section I.A.2: By no later than (1) month after the Effective Date, the Recipient shall establish and thereaftermaintain during the implementation of the Project a Project Steering Committee (PSC), with the composition, functions, staffing andresources satisfactory to the Association, and responsible for providing oversight and policy guidance to the Project. The PSCshall be co-chaired by the Under Secretaries of MoGEI and MoHEST and comprised of representative of State Education AdministrationBodies, Commission of Refugee Affairs (CRA), ministry in charge of Finance, UNHCR and the National Education Coalition (NEC).

Schedule 2 Section I.B.1(a): by no later than one (1) month after the Effective Date prepare and adopt in accordance with terms ofreference acceptable to the Association, a manual, which contains Project arrangements and procedures for: (i) institutionalcoordination and day-to-day implementation of the Project; (ii) monitoring, evaluation, reporting and communication; (iii) theperformance indicators; (iv) the reporting requirements on Project progress implementation including the timeline for reporting onany significant incident/accident in accordance with the ESCP; (v) arrangements for preventing, detecting, reporting,investigation, remediation and otherwise addressing fraud and corruption, including compliance with the Anti-Corruption Guidelines(which shall be annexed thereto); (vi) criteria, procedures and for female Stipend under Part 2.2 (c) selection; (vii) eligibilitycriteria for the selection of Eligible Teachers under Part 3.4 the Project; (viii) verification protocols and procedures forpayment of Salaries of Eligible Teachers; administration, procurement, financial management and accounting; (ix) the list ofExcluded Activities and (x) rules and procedures for processing and collection of Personal Data in accordance with national law onPersonal Data Protection if it is deemed adequate and good international practice.

Schedule 2 Section I.H: The Recipient shall no later than two (2) months from the Effective Date establish and thereafter maintainat all times during the implementation of the Project, a grievance redress mechanism, under terms and structure satisfactory to theAssociation.

title.narrative: Number of teachers certified on successful completion of teacher training programs

comment.narrative: This indicator will track the number of teachers receiving certificate upon successfully completing one of the below training programs: • Formal pre-service teacher training • Accelerated in-service training • Accelerated secondary Targets are cumulative. Progress Update: MoGEI has made significant progress in preparing for the Accelerated Secondary Education program, with the first batch of targeted teachers expected to commence training in November 2025. Progress has also been made in recruiting a TA firm to support Teacher Education reforms, with in-service teacher training anticipated to begin by March 2026.

Number of teachers recruited for the 200 re-operationalized schools in refugee hosting areas supported by the project.
Progress Update: Progress on this indicator is contingent upon the achievement of related activities, including the rehabilitation and re-operationalization of schools, as well as teacher recruitment, all of which are currently in the preparatory phase. Engagement of CSOs to support community mobilization and school management training is at an advanced stage.

title.narrative: Number of teachers benefitting from project-supported in-service teacher training

comment.narrative:
This indicator will measure the number of volunteer teachers who benefit from in-service teacher training programs
Progress Update: Progress on this indicator is contingent upon the achievement of related milestones, such as the review of the current in-service teacher training curriculum and practices. Preliminary supporting activities including the procurement of a technical assistance firm to support teacher education reforms have progressed well. In-service teacher training is anticipated to begin by March 2026.

title.narrative: Number of NTTI trainers and management team trained

comment.narrative:
This indicator will track the number of NTTIs trainers and staff trained. Targets are cumulative.
Progress Update: Progress on this indicator is contingent upon the re-operationalization of TTIs and the revision of pre-service and in-service teacher training curricula. To date, most activities have been preparatory, including the procurement of a technical assistance firm to support the strengthening of pre-service and in-service training.

title.narrative: Number of South Sudanese trainers trained to deliver digital agriculture program

comment.narrative:
This indicator will track the number of South Sudanese trainers that are trained to deliver the digital training for agriculture program. Targets are cumulative.
Progress Update: The training curriculum has been finalized and approved. MoHEST is currently in the process of identifying temporary training facilities within phase 1 universities, pending renovation works. Training of Trainers is anticipated to commence in December 2025.

title.narrative: Number of capacity development plans developed at the national sub-national levels

comment.narrative:
This indicator will track the number of capacity development plans prepared for the MoGEI and MoHEST at the national, state, and county levels (only for the counties where NTTIs are located). The respective entities should endorse these plans.
Progress Update: Progress on this indicator is dependent on the achievement of related activities, including the onboarding of TA firms to conduct the necessary assessments. The onboarding process is currently at an advanced stage in both Ministries.

title.narrative: Number of institutional assessments conducted at the national sub-national level

comment.narrative:
This indicator will track the number of capacity development plans prepared for the MoGEI and MoHEST at the national, state, and county levels (only for the counties where NTTIs are located). The respective entities should endorse these plans.
Progress Update: The onboarding of TA firms to support the preparation of these plans is at an advanced stage. Contracting of TA firms by both Ministries is expected to be completed by December 2025.

title.narrative: Number of teachers benefitting from project-supported accelerated secondary education programme for teachers

comment.narrative:
This indicator will track the number of existing teachers who have not completed secondary education that enroll in ASEP. Targets are cumulative.
Progress Update: MoGEI has made notable progress in preparing for ASEP. The first cohort of targeted teachers is expected to commence training in November 2025.

Progress Update: MoGEI has completed the identification of the 200 schools that will benefit from this project activity. Contracting for rehabilitation works is anticipated to commence within the next six months. comment.narrative:

Progress Update: Progress on this indicator is contingent upon the commencement and completion of actual student training, which is currently in the preparatory phase.

title.narrative: Number of re-operationalized schools in refugee hosting areas receiving school grants

Progress Update: Progress on this indicator is dependent on the achievement of related milestones, including the rehabilitation of schools, recruitment of teachers, and re-operationalization, all of which are currently in the preparatory phase. title.narrative: Number of students enrolled in project-supported formal pre-service teacher training

comment.narrative:

Progress Update: Progress on this indicator is dependent on the achievement of related milestones, such as the re-operationalization of the NTTIs. Preliminary supporting activities including engineering assessments of the TTIs and procurement of a technical assistance firm to support the review and strengthening of pre-service and in-service training have been progressing well.

title.narrative: Number of students enrolled in digital training for agriculture program

comment.narrative:
This indicator will track the number of students enrolled in the digital training for agriculture program. Targets are cumulative.
Progress Update: Notable progress has been made toward launching the digital skills training, with the curriculum now designed and approved. MoHEST anticipates commencing student training in February 2026.

Progress Update: Progress on this indicator is contingent upon the commencement of actual student training, which is currently in the preparatory phase. Measurement of student satisfaction will be possible once training activities begin.

comment.narrative:

Progress Update: Notable progress has been made towards launching the digital skills training, with the curriculum now designed and approved. MoHEST anticipates commencing student training in February 2026.

This indicator will track the number of NTTIs that have adequate facilities and staff and run regular teacher training programs.
Progress Update: Rehabilitation of NTTIs has not yet resumed; however, MoGEI has completed structural and engineering assessments of all NTTIs through a contracted design and supervision firm. Contracting for rehabilitation works is anticipated to begin in Phase 1 institutions by April 2026.

title.narrative: Evaluation of teacher training programs completed

comment.narrative: Evaluation of teacher training modalities conducted Progress Update: MoGEI is finalizing the onboarding of a technical assistance firm to conduct an evaluative assessment of the country's teacher training programs.

This indicator will track the development and endorsement by MoGEI of a national teacher policy. This policy will cover aspects such as teacher recruitment, deployment, professional development, and certification.
Progres Update: Progress on this indicator is contingent upon the achievement of related activities, notably the onboarding of TA to support pre-service and in-service teacher reforms. The onboarding process is currently at an advanced stage.

This indicator will track the implementation of the EMIS strengthening plan. The target will be achieved once the EMIS collects and reports data on at least 90% of schools in South Sudan including information on teachers (profile, qualifications, deployment and taining), schools (location, enrollment, physical facilities (including WASH, classrooms etc), teachers and school management committees and students.
Progress Update: Significant progress has been made on this indicator. An EMIS diagnosis has been carried out, and the EMIS Strengthening Business Requirements Plan has been prepared. A reformed Annual Education Census is currently being implemented, featuring revised tools, methodology, and training of MoGEI enumerators. This census will serve as one of the modules under a strengthened EMIS system.
